newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stagecoach buses into Scandinavia via Swebus.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach buses into Scandinavia via Swebus.

text.p: Britain's largest public transport group Stagecoach Holdings Plc on Tuesday announced the latest in an aggressive series of takeovers by acquiring Swebus, the leading bus operator in the Nordic region.
"We've concluded that this is the most efficient state-owned business that we've looked at," Stagecoach Executive Chairman Brian Souter told a news conference.

Stagecoach, whose strong-arm competition tactics have been widely criticised by politicians, unions and media in Britain and Sweden alike, will pay 2.4 billion crowns ($361.6 million) for Swebus and will take over 1.18 billion crowns in company debt.
Swebus's current owner, state railways company Statens Jarnvagar (SJ), said it was extremely pleased with the terms of the deal.
"We believe an industrial buyer is the best solution, partly for Swebus's further development, and partly so that we could get the best price for the company," SJ said in a statement.
Through the takeover, Stagecoach becomes the leading player on the Nordic bus market.
Its 6,200 employees and 3,400 buses operate throughout the region, a platform it will use for further expansion into Europe, Souter said.
"I won't say we're not looking to go further," he said, but declined to comment on where the Scotland-based transport company with head offices in Perth might be headed next.
"Absolutely not. We're hoping to get there before some of our competitors," he said. "We've always done better business were there are less sheep and more people".
The Swebus takeover is the latest in a long string of Souter-masterminded acquisitions that has seen Stagecoach's market value grow to 1.25 billion pounds sterling ($2 billion) in just 16 years.

The company announced in late July its intention to buy Porterbrook, a leasing company that owns a third of Britain's passenger railway rolling stock, but Souter said SJ had nothing to fear from its former subsidiary.
"We've shown that coach companies and rail companies have been complementary operations. There's plenty of room for everyone in the market," he said.
Speculation in the Swedish media that Stagecoach would slash jobs in the Swedish bus company were unfounded, Souter said.

"One can always make some improvements but we have to get a better understanding of the operation first. Swebus has fewer employees per bus even than Stagecoach, so maybe we should bring their management into the U.K.," he said. ($ = 6.637 Swedish Crowns) ($ = 0.640 British Pounds Sterling)
